content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported three deaths in infants under 12 months of age in the United States that were linked to the use of cough and cold medications. Medical examiners or coroners determined these medications to be the underlying cause of death. This highlights the importance of healthcare providers exercising caution when prescribing, and caregivers being cautious when administering, cough and cold medications to children under 2 years of age. For further details, visit the FDA website. Codeine is a medication commonly used in combination with other drugs to suppress coughing. It is also prescribed to alleviate mild to moderate pain. In some cases, it may be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Codeine is available as a standalone medication or in combination with other drugs in the form of tablets, capsules, or liquid. It is typically taken orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take codeine exactly as prescribed. Be aware that codeine has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take a larger dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than directed by your doctor. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before measuring your dose. Before taking codeine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to codeine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including other pain relievers, antidepressants, medications for cough, cold, or allergies, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver, kidney, or lung disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking codeine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking codeine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how codeine affects you. Additionally, alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking codeine. If you are taking codeine as needed, you may not have a regular dosing schedule. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take codeine on a regular basis and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Codeine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: dizziness, lightheadedness, drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, rash, or difficulty urinating. If you experience severe side effects such as difficulty breathing or mood changes, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store codeine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Codeine is available under various brand names, including Brontex®, Cheracol® with Codeine Syrup, Gani-Tuss® NR, Guiatuss AC® Syrup, Guiatussin® with Codeine, HaNew Riversin® AC, Mytussin® AC Cough Syrup, Robafen AC® Syrup, Robitussin A-C® Syrup, and Tussi-Organidin® NR, among others. There are also combination products containing codeine, such as Ambenyl® Cough Syrup, Bromanyl® Cough Syrup, Codimal® PH Syrup, Colrex® Compound, Cycofed® Expectorant, Decohistine® DH, Dihistine® DH Elixir, Guaifenesin DAC®, Guiatuss DAC® Syrup, KG-Fed® Expectorant Syrup, Mytussin® DAC, Novahistine® DH, Nucofed®, Pediacof® Cough Syrup, Phenergan® VC with Codeine Syrup, Robitussin®-DAC, Ryna-C®, Triacin-C® Cough Syrup, and many others. These products often combine codeine with other active ingredients such as guaifenesin, pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine, or promethazine.
